content: Surface mining operations require expansive and highly reliable communication networks capable of covering vast geographic areas while maintaining high data throughput and low latency. Technologies such as private 5G networks, Long-Term Evolution systems, and industrial Wi-Fi are critical components of this infrastructure [34] . These connectivity solutions facilitate the deployment of autonomous haulage systems and remotely operated vehicles, which depend entirely on seamless, high-bandwidth communication networks to ensure real-time data transmission and safe operation [7] . The dynamic nature of surface mines, where heavy machinery and personnel are in constant motion, demands an infrastructure that can seamlessly hand over connections without signal degradation. The increasing reliance on autonomous equipment and artificial intelligence-driven processes requires an infrastructure capable of integrating massive influxes of sensor data, controlling machinery remotely, and processing vast quantities of information for instantaneous decision-making . The deployment of private 5G and advanced Wi-Fi networks in these subterranean environments is critical for supporting the continuous data flows required by modern mining technologies [35] . Underground operations rely heavily on digital twins and predictive maintenance protocols, which are grounded in artificial intelligence and machine learning [7] . These applications require uninterrupted data flows from deep within the mine to surface-level control centers, further underscoring the critical role of advanced, uninterrupted connectivity . Without a resilient underground communication backbone, the real-time monitoring of structural integrity, air quality, and equipment health—all vital for miner safety and operational continuity—would be severely compromised. For instance, alliances such as the partnership between Ericsson and Epiroc, which expanded in June 2026, were specifically aimed at accelerating mining digitalization by leveraging 5G technology [35] . This suggests that ongoing initiatives throughout the early 2020s were highly focused on improving connectivity and operational efficiency within mining environments . Furthermore, historical precedents, such as Gold Fields’ investment pledge of 1.714 billion ZAR for mining infrastructure expansion in 2016, illustrate the industry's long-term commitment to sectoral growth and technological modernization [32] .
